title: A Comet Does Not Need Chasing

segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Pause somewhere safe. This is for observing an ordinary urge, not replacing help in an immediate safety or medical situation.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Name what is here: craving... pulling... wanting. Imagine it as a comet entering the edge of your sky.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Locate the urge in the body. Notice pressure, heat, tightness, movement, or restless energy.
[soft, slow, warm voice] The comet can be bright without giving instructions. Watch its tail, speed, and changing shape.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice any thought that says now, always, or impossible. Let the words travel behind the comet rather than steering your body.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] Intensity may rise. A brighter moment does not mean you must chase it or make it disappear.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Rate the urge from zero to ten, then check again after several breaths. Observe change without demanding reduction.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel the body beneath the sky: feet, seat, hands, breath. You are more than the streak of light passing through.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice whether the urge has moved, sharpened, faded, or stayed. All are useful observations.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] Choice can wait until the comet is no longer filling the whole window. Remain here for a few more breaths.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Let the comet continue beyond the horizon. Return to the room and choose the next action deliberately.
